title: Why Do Dogs Lick You?
description:
It's not just affection — there's real chemistry behind it.

script: Every time your dog licks you, they're actually getting a small hit of dopamine and endorphins, the same feel-good chemicals we get from a hug. Licking is one of the first bonding behaviors puppies learn, from their mother grooming them to littermates licking each other to build trust. When your dog licks you, they're doing the same thing, reinforcing the bond and picking up information about you through taste and smell at the same time. It can also be a calming behavior, something dogs do to soothe themselves when they're excited or a little stressed. So that lick on your hand isn't random, it's your dog's built-in love language, chemically wired for connection.
